body: # Philadelphia Fed – 2nd Quarter 2026 Survey Of Professional Forecasters. The Philadelphia Fed 2nd Quarter 2026 Survey of Professional Forecasters was released on May 15, 2026. This survey is somewhat unique in various regards, such as it incorporates a longer time frame for various measures. The survey shows, among many measures, the following median expectations:. Regarding the risk of a negative quarter in real GDP in any of the next few quarters, mean estimates are 17.9%, 25.1%, 24.5%, 25.7%, and 23.0% for each of the quarters from Q2 2026 through Q2 2027, respectively. As well, there are also a variety of time frames shown (present quarter through the year 2035) with the median expected inflation (annualized) of each. Over all time frames expectations are shown to be in the 2.1% to 6.0% range. However, as those familiar with this site are aware, I do not agree with many of the consensus estimates and much of the commentary in these forecast surveys.

*   [1 Headline HICP inflation expectations revised upwards in the near term, while longer-term expectations remained close to 2%](https://www.ecb.europa.eu/stats/ecb_surveys/survey_of_professional_forecasters/html/ecb.spf2026q2.en.html#toc3). *   [2 Longer-term inflation expectations remain well anchored](https://www.ecb.europa.eu/stats/ecb_surveys/survey_of_professional_forecasters/html/ecb.spf2026q2.en.html#toc4). Expectations for core inflation, as measured by the HICP excluding energy and food (HICPX), were also revised upwards in the near term**.**[[1](https://www.ecb.europa.eu/stats/ecb_surveys/survey_of_professional_forecasters/html/ecb.spf2026q2.en.html#footnote.1)]. **In this round, SPF respondents were asked special questions relating to the impact of the war in the Middle East.**First, they were asked to indicate, for each calendar year horizon from 2026 to 2030, the impact of the war on their baseline expectations for headline inflation, core inflation and wage growth, and whether it represented an upside, balanced or downside risk to those baseline projections.[[2](https://www.ecb.europa.eu/stats/ecb_surveys/survey_of_professional_forecasters/html/ecb.spf2026q2.en.html#footnote.2)]. **Longer-term inflation expectations were unchanged at 2.0% with most respondents continuing to see headline inflation at 2.0% in 2030.**[[4](https://www.ecb.europa.eu/stats/ecb_surveys/survey_of_professional_forecasters/html/ecb.spf2026q2.en.html#footnote.4)]. [](https://www.ecb.europa.eu/stats/ecb_surveys/survey_of_professional_forecasters/html/ecb.spf2026q2.en.html)For the tenth consecutive round, more than half of the respondents reported longer-term inflation expectations of 2.0%. # [](https://www.ecb.europa.eu/stats/ecb_surveys/survey_of_professional_forecasters/html/ecb.spf2026q2.en.html)4 Joint revisions in inflation and growth expectations point to an inflationary and growth-dampening shock of limited duration.
